name: DVWA: Command Injection to Shell
short_description: Exploit command injection in DVWA to get a reverse shell on the web server.
description: DVWA (Damn Vulnerable Web Application) has a command injection vulnerability in the 'ping' functionality. We'll exploit this to execute arbitrary commands and get a reverse shell. This teaches OS command injection - OWASP Top 10 #1.

steps.title: Open DVWA in browser
steps.explanation: Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser. Default login: admin/password. Set security to 'Low' in DVWA Security settings.

steps.title: Navigate to Command Injection
steps.explanation: Click 'Command Injection' in the left menu. This page lets you ping an IP. It's supposed to just ping, but we can inject commands.

steps.title: Test command injection
steps.explanation: Enter this in the IP field. The semicolon terminates the ping command and runs 'id'.
steps.expected: You should see ping output PLUS 'uid=33(www-data)'

steps.title: Set up a listener in Kali
steps.explanation: Start a Netcat listener on port 4444 to catch our reverse shell. Keep this terminal open - it will wait for a connection.

steps.title: Send reverse shell payload (in browser)
steps.explanation: Enter this in the DVWA form and submit. Check your Netcat terminal - you should see a connection!

steps.title: Verify shell access (no prompt - just type!)
steps.explanation: Back in Netcat terminal: There is NO prompt - cursor just blinks. Type 'id' and press Enter anyway!

steps.title: Upgrade to interactive shell
steps.explanation: Now you get a real prompt! If python3 fails, try 'python' instead.

steps.title: Explore the web root
steps.explanation: Browse the web application files. Look for config files with database credentials.

steps.title: Read database config
steps.explanation: Extract database credentials for further access.

success_criteria: You have a shell on the DVWA container as www-data. You can read files and explore the system.
